title: The Rich Man and the Tanner
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Rich Man took up his residence next door to a Tanner, and found the smell of the tan-yard so extremely unpleasant that he told him he must go. The Tanner delayed his departure, and the Rich Man had to speak to him several times about it; and every time the Tanner said he was making arrangements to move very shortly. This went on for some time, till at last the Rich Man got so used to the smell that he ceased to mind it, and troubled the Tanner with his objections no more.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who moves in next door to the Tanner?
options: A young farmer
A traveling merchant
A Rich Man
A retired soldier

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Rich Man find unpleasant?
options: The smell of the tan-yard
The noise from the Tanner's workshop
The Tanner's rude manner
The state of the Tanner's fence

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Rich Man tell the Tanner he must do?
options: Cover the smell with perfume
Pay a fine for the smell
Work only at certain hours
Go, meaning leave the area

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Tanner say each time the Rich Man complains?
options: That he had no intention of ever moving
That he was making arrangements to move very shortly
That the smell would go away on its own
That the Rich Man should move instead

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what eventually happens to the Rich Man's reaction to the smell?
options: He becomes seriously ill because of it
He moves away himself to escape it
He gets so used to it that he ceases to mind it
He starts to enjoy the smell over time

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Rich Man stop doing once he grows used to the smell?
options: Troubling the Tanner with his objections
Visiting the Tanner's shop
Paying his rent on time
Speaking to any of his neighbors

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Tanner keep delaying his move rather than simply refusing outright?
options: He genuinely intends to move as soon as possible
He is waiting for a better property to become available
He does not understand why the smell bothers the Rich Man
Promising to move soon lets him avoid conflict while never actually needing to act

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Rich Man's changed reaction reveal about how people respond to constant exposure to something unpleasant?
options: People never truly get used to unpleasant smells over time
Repeated exposure can wear down a strong initial objection until it no longer bothers a person
The Rich Man secretly enjoyed the smell from the beginning
The Tanner must have improved the smell without saying so

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "departure" mean in "The Tanner delayed his departure"?
options: His work each day
His payment of rent
His act of leaving
His conversation with neighbors

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Given enough time, people can grow accustomed to almost anything, even what once seemed intolerable
Rich men are always more sensitive to smells than working people
Tanners should be required to live far from other neighborhoods
Complaining repeatedly is the best way to force someone to change

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how many times does the Rich Man have to speak to the Tanner about moving?
options: Only once
Every single day
Only after a year had passed
Several times

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how long does this situation continue before the Rich Man stops minding the smell?
options: For a single week
For some time
For only a few hours
Until the Tanner apologized

questions.prompt: According to the passage, does the Tanner ever actually move away?
options: Yes, he moves within a few days
Yes, but only after the Rich Man moved first
No, the passage never describes him actually moving
No, because the Rich Man forced him to stay

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the Tanner have felt no urgency to actually follow through on his promise?
options: The Rich Man's complaints eventually stopped entirely, removing any pressure to act
The smell of the tan-yard had genuinely improved over time
The Rich Man offered to pay for the Tanner's moving costs
The Tanner had already found a buyer for his property

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the outcome suggest about the Rich Man's original demand that the Tanner "must go"?
options: It was eventually enforced by local authorities
It caused a lasting conflict between the two neighbors
It was withdrawn immediately after being made
It turned out not to be as urgent or necessary as he first believed

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Rich Man "ceased to mind" the smell?
options: He stopped noticing anything at all
He stopped being bothered by it
He stopped living in his house
He stopped speaking to his neighbors

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Tanner is forced by law to close his business
A Rich Man moves away rather than tolerate the smell
A Rich Man demands his neighbor move away from an unpleasant smell, but eventually grows used to it and stops complaining
A Tanner successfully improves the smell of his tan-yard
